# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

S1 Add a `significantDigits` option to pretty-bytes so callers can change the default rounding from 3 significant digits, with readme, types, and tests updated. (Nov 2, 10:06 PM)
**Investigated**: The pretty-bytes `index.js` rounding path, including the default `toPrecision` branch that hardcodes 3 significant digits and the `buildLocaleOptions` gate that selects it. The readme and `index.d.ts` option docs, and the layout of `test.js` and `index.test-d.ts`. The first `npm test` run after the edits, which failed on xo lint: a complexity warning on `prettyBytes`, trailing spaces in `index.d.ts`, and an ava assertion-argument error at `test.js:1212`.

**Learned**: The default rounding only runs when neither `minimumFractionDigits` nor `maximumFractionDigits` is set, so `significantDigits` must be gated on that same condition. Existing fraction-digit options throw on bad input, while the new option falls back silently to 3. The docs and typings are kept in sync by hand across readme, JSDoc, and tsd tests.

**Completed**: `significantDigits` was added in `index.js` with a `resolveSignificantDigits` helper that accepts integers from 1 to 100 and otherwise returns 3. Documentation was added to `readme.md` and `index.d.ts`, a type test to `index.test-d.ts`, and three runtime tests to `test.js`. Trailing whitespace in `index.d.ts` was stripped and the assertion message was changed to a template string. The latest `npm test` run passed with 54 tests passing and 3 skipped. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: The session is waiting on a decision about whether invalid `significantDigits` values should throw, as `fixedWidth` does, or keep the silent fallback to 3. Follow-up work depends on that choice. The complexity warning on `prettyBytes` (22 against a limit of 20) is still open, though it is reported as a warning rather than an error.

**Notes**: The silent fallback follows the existing guidance that new options should not throw on bad values, so the user may want to confirm it. The complexity warning appeared in the lint output, and the later passing run does not show whether `index.js` was changed to address it. The `significantDigits` tests cover the 1 to 4 digit range, unit rollover, locale, bits, forced units, the fraction-digit override, and invalid input.
